evals.prompt: Review the Content panel (editor right-panel config) for the Split the Points slide type. The 'Total budget' field shows its explanation/current value only as a hover-state readout that pops up when you hover the field — there is no ? help icon next to the label.
evals.expected_output: FAILs C3 (help text is the exception; explanation lives in a ? tooltip). A setting's explanation must live in the standard ? help tooltip placed right after the label and reachable on hover, keyboard focus, AND tap — not a bespoke hover-state readout that keyboard and touch users can't reach and that is never the sole home of the information. Fix: add the shared ? tooltip on the 'Total budget' label and drop the ad-hoc hover value. All other criteria may pass; overall NEEDS FIX.
evals.label: bad-example
evals.notes: Real bug AHA-46438 (Split the Points). The total-budget value's info was surfaced as a hover state instead of the standard ? tooltip. Sourced from the AHA-46123 QA batch as a BAD example for the settings judge.

evals.prompt: Review the Content panel for Split the Points. The ? help icon next to 'Your question' is a different glyph AND a different size from the ? icons on the other settings, and its tooltip points a different direction from the rest.
evals.expected_output: FAILs C3 (consistency clause). Every ? in one panel must be the same shared-component glyph at the same size with the same tooltip placement — mixed help icons, mixed sizes, or inconsistent up/down tooltip direction read as unfinished. Fix: pull every ? from the shared icon component (aha-design-icons) sized to the setting-name text, with one consistent tooltip direction. Overall NEEDS FIX.
evals.label: bad-example
evals.notes: Real bugs AHA-46489 + AHA-46544 (Split the Points) — the Content panel shipped two different ? glyphs and mismatched icon sizes / tooltip directions. BAD example for C3's consistency rule.

evals.prompt: Review the 'Total budget' numeric input in the Split the Points config. It accepts any number of digits (no maxlength), accepts letters and symbols, and only snaps back into the allowed 10–1000 range when the creator types something invalid on purpose and then clicks outside the box.
evals.expected_output: FAILs C10 (numeric/stepper config-input contract). A numeric config input must: cap its length (mirror Poll's 4-digit cap), accept numbers only, clamp to its min/max with an IMMEDIATE fallback on change/blur (not only on deliberate misuse), and ship pre-filled with the recommended default. Fix all four. Overall NEEDS FIX.
evals.label: bad-example
evals.notes: Real bug AHA-46440 (Split the Points). Total-budget input had no maxlength, no numbers-only rule, and only fell back on blur after intentional bad input. BAD example for the C10 numeric-input contract added from this ticket.
assertions: Overall verdict is NEEDS FIX
C10 is marked FAIL
Flags the missing length/maxlength cap on the numeric input
Flags that the input must accept numbers only (reject letters/symbols)
Flags that min/max clamping must be immediate (on change/blur), not only after deliberate bad input

Option rows must show a neutral placeholder matching an equivalent existing slide type (Poll uses 'Option 1', 'Option 2'), and a placeholder is NEVER treated as real content — an option still holding its placeholder must not render downstream. Fix: add the 'Option N' placeholders and gate canvas rendering on a real value. Overall NEEDS FIX.
evals.label: bad-example
evals.notes: Real bug AHA-46484 (Split the Points). Missing option placeholders and placeholder-rendered-as-real-content. BAD example for the C10 placeholder rule.
assertions: Overall verdict is NEEDS FIX
C10 is marked FAIL
Flags the missing option placeholder (should be 'Option 1/2', mirroring an existing slide type)
Flags that a placeholder must not be rendered as real content downstream

evals.notes: Real bug AHA-46562 (Split the Points). Wrong default and wrong option order in the measurement-unit select. BAD example for C12's select-default/order rule.

Flags that percent should be ordered first (most-relevant-first), not last

evals.prompt: Review this AI-generated right panel. Every setting has an always-visible help line under its name: 'Mark a correct answer' — 'Reveal the right choice after the vote.'; 'Result chart' — 'Only bar charts show option images.'; 'Allow multiple choices' — 'Off means one pick per person.'; 'Show percentages' — 'Display % instead of raw vote counts.'; 'Presenter note' — 'Optional context shown under the question on the canvas.'; 'Reset' — 'Put the starter options back.' Each setting ALSO has a small circled info icon (ⓘ) next to its name.
evals.expected_output: FAILs C3 on three counts. (1) Panel-level help-text anti-pattern — nearly every setting carries a help line; help text must be near-absent (default zero). Every line here is descriptive, not a must-see irreversible consequence, so each moves into the ? tooltip or is deleted; 'Put the starter options back.' becomes nothing (or, if Reset discards edits, help text stating THAT loss). (2) Redundancy — settings carry both a help icon AND a help line (same explanation twice); keep the tooltip, drop the line. (3) Wrong glyph — the help trigger is an info icon (ⓘ); it must be the shared question-mark (?) help glyph. Overall NEEDS FIX.
evals.label: bad-example
evals.notes: Classic AI over-help-text panel: help line on every setting, info (ⓘ) icons instead of ? glyphs, and both channels stacked on one setting. Reported by Lan from a generated settings panel. BAD example for C3 (panel-level default, redundancy, and wrong glyph).
assertions: Overall verdict is NEEDS FIX (not OK TO SHIP)
C3 is marked FAIL
Flags the panel-level help-text overuse: a help line on every/most settings is the anti-pattern; descriptions belong in the ? tooltip
Flags that the tooltip trigger is an info icon (ⓘ) and must be a question-mark (?) glyph
Flags the redundancy of a setting carrying both a help icon AND a help-text line

evals.prompt: Review the option list in a generated right panel. The rows look right (drag handle, colour dot, text input, Image button, delete), but the '+ Add option' button beneath them is a small button hugged to the left at content width, not spanning the panel.

evals.label: bad-example
evals.notes: Reported by Lan — the '+ Add option' button rendered hug-left instead of full-width, breaking the aligned single-column read of the panel. BAD example for C10's full-width '+ Add' rule.
assertions: Overall verdict is NEEDS FIX
C10 is marked FAIL
Flags that the '+ Add' button must span the full panel width, not hug content width on one side

evals.prompt: Review the corrected panel: each setting shows only its noun-phrase name with a single question-mark (?) help glyph after it (no help-text lines) except 'Response limit', which keeps one help line stating the must-see consequence ('New responses are blocked once the limit is reached.'); the '+ Add option' button spans the full panel width.
evals.expected_output: C3 and C10 PASS; overall OK TO SHIP. The panel has near-zero help text (one justified must-see-consequence line), no redundant icon+line pairs, ? (not ⓘ) glyphs, and a full-width '+ Add'. The judge must not invent fails on a correctly-restrained panel.
evals.label: good-control
evals.notes: Positive control for the help-text/glyph/full-width fixes (counterpart to evals 8 and 9). Ensures the judge accepts a panel that keeps exactly one justified help line and moves everything else into ? tooltips.

C11 (and/or C10) is marked FAIL

Flags the always-visible delete (must be on row hover only)

evals.prompt: Review a poll option row. An outer bordered row contains, from the left OUTSIDE the input, a drag handle; then a separately-bordered text input holding a selection checkbox and the label; and a bordered delete button pinned at the top-right that is always visible. Diff it against the shipped Ranking slide's option row.
evals.expected_output: FAILs C10 on the STRUCTURE — not the checkbox. The row div itself must BE the single bordered input with a borderless textarea inside; here it is a box-in-a-box (row wrapping a separately-bordered input). The drag handle must be the first child INSIDE that one border, not a column to its left. The delete must float just outside the top-right on HOVER, not sit always-visible. The selection checkbox is a legitimate per-type feature for a scored poll — do NOT flag it. Fix: collapse to one border (row = input, textarea borderless), move the drag handle inside, make the delete hover-only. Overall NEEDS FIX.
evals.label: bad-example
assertions: Overall verdict is NEEDS FIX
C10 is marked FAIL
Flags the drag handle placed outside/left of the input (must be first child inside the one border)
Flags the double border — an outer row wrapping a separately-bordered input (the row div itself is the single input; textarea borderless)
Flags the always-visible delete (must be hover-only, floating just outside the top-right)
Does NOT flag the selection checkbox — it is a legitimate per-type feature for a scored poll
evals.notes: Real bug from another repo's Claude generating a poll-style option row (reported by Lan): drag handle outside the input, a double border, and an always-visible delete. The checkbox/colour dot are legitimate per-type poll features and must NOT be flagged — only the structural core (frame, handle, delete) must match Ranking.

A plain setting — especially a lone toggle row — sits directly on the panel surface, separated from its neighbours by spacing tokens; it must NOT be wrapped in a card or any container with its own background/tinted fill or border. A filled pill reads as a selectable object, not a configuration row. Fix: drop the tinted container and separate with spacing. Overall NEEDS FIX.

evals.prompt: Review a scoring settings panel where several setting labels have a topically-relevant leading icon: a star before 'Scoring', a star before 'Points', a trophy before 'Leaderboard', and a clock before 'Time limit'. Explicitly rejects the 'topically relevant / meaningful, so it's fine' rationalization — a topical icon is still decorative, not functional
